source.title: The Anxiety of Influence: Bloom Filters in Transformer Attention Heads

page_placements.theme: Published head classes have broader, context-dependent functions

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether heads identified as IOI duplicate-token heads also process repeated tokens beyond names and contribute to broader processing, using behavioral measurements and ablation rather than IOI circuit faithfulness tests.
record.gate_note: The paper reports no experiment testing the 26-head IOI circuit on IOI performance. Its relevant results concern the overlap with IOI duplicate-token heads, token-repetition generalization, and ablation effects on perplexity. The CPU/MPS IOI benchmark result is a backend validation, not a test of the circuit. Cross-model Bloom-filter results do not test whether the IOI circuit carries IOI in those models.
record.test_reason: The study checks whether heads it matches to IOI duplicate-token heads in GPT-2 small attend to repeated tokens beyond names, in generic sentences and WikiText. This bears only on V3's 'components reused for other tasks' part. It runs no IOI-circuit experiment: no IOI faithfulness, backup or cross-model IOI test. Its perplexity ablations measure general language-modelling contribution, not reuse in the same role.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. More precisely: the three genuine membership-testing heads are the top-ranked duplicate-token heads by duplicate-token score (ranks 1, 2 and 4). They respond to any repeated token, not just names. Under mean ablation, the authors' primary method, they contribute to both repeated and novel token processing, so they are not functionally modular.
record.recipe_differences: The paper measures attention to repeated tokens and ablates heads while tracking perplexity on repeat and no-repeat sentences; it does not trace or ablate the full IOI circuit using IOI performance as the outcome.
record.method_sensitivity: Ablation conclusions differ by method: zero ablation shows a repeat-specific interaction (+14.6%), while mean ablation shows a −3.7% interaction and a larger effect on no-repeat sentences.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean-ablating the three Bloom/duplicate-score heads raises perplexity on both repeat (+9.3%) and no-repeat (+13.0%) sentences. There is no repeat-specific interaction under mean ablation (−3.7%), but there is one under zero ablation (+14.6%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI-associated duplicate-token heads are not functionally specific to repetition and contribute to general next-token prediction; conclusions depend on the ablation type.

record.peer_reviewed: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023)
record.problems: The ablation results are method-sensitive; the authors caution that zero ablation is less principled and that its control comparison has extreme variance. The broader-processing ablation results use perplexity on repeat/no-repeat sentences, not IOI task performance.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant, separately reported outcomes were omitted.

untested.parts: The 26-head circuit, its 7 classes, and faithfulness, completeness and minimality on IOI.

IOI circuits in other models, sizes or checkpoints. The cross-model Bloom-head counts do not involve IOI. Reuse of components other than duplicate-token-like heads, and reuse in a specific downstream task, are also untested.
Other circuit-finding methods or metrics recovering the IOI circuit.
IOI-circuit faithfulness or completeness under different ablations, metrics or prompt distributions.
IOI across name orders, templates or more names.

missing.what: Overlap ranking by the IOI duplicate-token score: L0H5 rank 1, L0H1 rank 2, L1H11 rank 4. L3H0 ranks 50th of 144, although head 3.0 is one of Wang et al.'s duplicate-token heads.
missing.versions: V3 (component identity); possibly relevant to V1's head assignment, though it uses a different score and stimuli, not path patching

record.verdict_notes: This is a single-author preprint. It carries a NeurIPS 2023 footer but is dated 2026, so the record's peer_reviewed field is likely wrong. The appendix IOI logit difference (+3.36 CPU vs −0.99 MPS) is a backend check, not a circuit result. The Bloom heads only partly coincide with the IOI circuit's duplicate-token heads: only L0H1 is shared, and IOI's 3.0 ranks 50th here. This weakens the link of r1 and r2 to IOI components.

versions.untested_parts: The IOI circuit, its 26 heads and 7 classes, faithfulness, completeness, minimality, and effects of removing everything outside it.
Whether backup heads take over the main name-mover heads' role after ablation.

Whether the same IOI circuit and roles carry IOI in other models, sizes, or checkpoints. The study tests reuse/generalization of IOI duplicate-token heads beyond name repetition in GPT-2 small, but not their reuse for other specific tasks or their IOI role in other models.
Whether other circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics recover the IOI circuit.

Whether IOI circuit faithfulness or completeness depends on ablation, metric, or IOI prompt distribution. The study compares ablation methods on repeated-token processing, not IOI circuit performance.
IOI performance across name orders, templates, or numbers of names.

source_check.notes: The source retains inconsistent three-versus-four-head descriptions following L3H0's reclassification. The NeurIPS 2023 footer in this 2026 preprint does not independently establish reviewed publication status.

statements.correction: Section 5.1: L0H1, L0H5 and L1H11 have duplicate-token-score ranks 2, 1 and 4; generalization index 0.70 versus 0.49; non-name repetition attention 0.276 versus 0.099. Original-circuit overlap restricted to L0H1: not independently established in the supplied text. Appendix D: IOI backend sanity check during related work; no IOI circuit faithfulness, completeness or backup-head experiment.
statements.problem: The broader non-name repetition result and duplicate-score selection are supported. The supplied study does not establish that only L0H1 belonged to the original IOI duplicate-token group. Appendix D also reports an IOI backend sanity check, so an unqualified claim of no IOI capability check needs clarification.

statements.correction: Table 6: four-head comparison; mean-ablation repeat change +9.3%, no-repeat change +13.0%, interaction −3.7%; zero-ablation interaction +14.6%. The pooled ablation set is not explicitly enumerated after L3H0's reclassification.
statements.problem: The perplexity changes and ablation-method dependence are correct, but attribution to three heads conflicts with Table 6's four-head comparison.
